name: @w6w-apps/segment
description: Send identify, track, page, group, alias and batch calls to Segment's Tracking API.

w6w.longDescription:
Segment's Tracking API is the write side of a customer-data pipeline, and this app implements its full verb set: identify a person by their traits, track a named event, record a page view, associate a user with a group or account, alias two identities together as one, and batch up to 2,500 of any of those calls into a single request. Free-form trait, property and context objects pass straight through to Segment untouched, so the wire shape a workflow builds is exactly what Segment receives.

Segment splits its API in two — a write-only Tracking API for events and a separate, bearer-authenticated config API for managing sources and warehouses — and this app deliberately calls only the Tracking API, so it has nothing to say about workspace configuration. Every call is idempotent: a message id derived from the invocation is attached to each event, so a host's retry of the same run lands on Segment's own deduplication window rather than double-recording it.

The write key is sent as HTTP Basic with an empty password, and the Tracking API has no dedicated ping endpoint of its own — the connection test instead sends a harmless identify call against a fixed anonymous id, so repeated checks update one throwaway profile rather than minting a new one each time.
